nodes.title: Deep Learning for RF Device Fingerprinting in Cognitive Communication Networks
nodes.dataset: 7 commercial ZigBee Pro devices operating in the 2.4 GHz band, with random 32-byte payloads generated in MATLAB.
nodes.methodology: A convolutional neural network (CNN) trained on time-domain complex baseband error signals to classify devices based on unique physical-layer signatures, with frequency correction applied to remove carrier offset.
nodes.contribution: Proposed a CNN-based framework for RF fingerprinting using time-domain error signals, enabling device identification without relying on cryptographic keys or MAC addresses.

nodes.title: Release Note: WiFi RF Datasets for Device Fingerprinting Using Deep Learning
nodes.dataset: 1.2TB of WiFi transmissions from 50 devices over 5 days (indoor/outdoor), with 5 transmissions per device. Files stored in SigMF format with metadata including sampling rate, timestamps, and carrier frequency.
nodes.methodology: Data collected using 50 Pycom devices and Ettus USRP B210 receivers, capturing I/Q samples at 25MS/s. GNURadio configured for signal processing and metadata storage in SigMF format.
nodes.contribution: Provides standardized WiFi datasets with SigMF metadata for research on device fingerprinting and RF signal analysis.

nodes.title: Deep Learning Based RF Fingerprint Identification Using Differential Constellation Trace Figure
nodes.dataset: 54 ZigBee devices with varying SNR levels (15 dB and 30 dB) for classification.
nodes.methodology: DCTF converts time-series signal data into 2D images representing differential relationships. A CNN is trained to classify devices based on DCTF features without prior synchronization information.
nodes.contribution: Proposed DCTF-CNN method with zero prior synchronization, high accuracy, and low complexity for RFF identification.

nodes.title: Few-Shot Speciﬁc Emitter Identiﬁcation via Deep Metric Ensemble Learning
nodes.dataset: Massive ADS-B signal samples for offline training, few-shot samples from new aircraft for online deployment.
nodes.methodology: Proposes DMEL with feature embedding via complex-valued CVCNN and metric learning (triplet loss, center loss), combined with ensemble classifiers for improved generalization.
nodes.contribution: Introduces offline feature embedding and online classifier paradigm, metric learning for generalized features, and ensemble learning for enhanced performance.

nodes.title: Semi-Supervised RF Fingerprinting with Consistency-Based Regularization
nodes.dataset: Simulated and real-world datasets (specific names not provided)
nodes.methodology: The paper proposes a semi-supervised learning framework combining data augmentation, consistency-based regularization, and pseudo-labeling. A composite data augmentation scheme, including stochastic permutation and signal rotation, is designed for radio signals to enhance generalization.
nodes.contribution: 1. Comprehensive analysis of data augmentation techniques for RF fingerprinting. 2. Novel composite data augmentation scheme (stochastic permutation + signal rotation). 3. End-to-end semi-supervised framework combining consistency-based regularization and pseudo-labeling.

Both papers address device/emitter identification using deep learning but differ in methodology (CNN vs. DMEL with metric/ensemble learning), dataset (ZigBee Pro vs. ADS-B), and task focus (general classification vs. few-shot learning).

They share the task of classification but differ in approach and dataset usage.

Paper 1 focuses on WiFi device fingerprinting with SigMF datasets, while Paper 2 addresses few-shot emitter identification using ADS-B signals and metric learning. No direct overlap in methods or datasets.
